hints.title: Prime Factor Limitation
hints.text: Because every valid digit is between 1 and 9, the divisor t can only consist of prime factors 2, 3, 5, and 7. If t contains any other prime factor, return -1.

hints.title: Factor Packing
hints.text: To minimize the number of digits needed for a set of prime factors, greedily combine factor 2 into 8, factor 3 into 9, factors 2 and 3 into 6, and pairs of 2 into 4.

hints.title: Pivot Exploration
hints.text: Traverse backwards from the end of num. Try to increment the digit at the pivot position if the remaining space can accommodate all leftover required factors.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Greedy right-to-left prefix backtracking packing remaining prime factors into minimal digits.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Length of num up to 200,000 rules out numerical trial or basic combinatorial enumeration.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Factorizes t into single-digit primes and packs leftover factor counts greedily into 8, 9, 6, etc.
